page: Amazon Web Services c6in.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 3.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI.

The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring external EBS volumes for persistent disk storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results highlight average single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core Geekbench score of 1518.0 and single-core stress-ng score of 1889.09 rank in the middle 50% tier, supported by solid single-threaded compression speeds such as gzip compression at 27.68 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench multi-core result of 3252.0 and PassMark CPU score of 5845.97. Memory subsystem testing shows weak to poor bandwidth, logging 29.04 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and a PassMark memory score of 1030.18.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6in.xlarge balances dedicated compute capacity with a high baseline network interface, though the low memory ceiling and reliance on EBS storage limit scalability for data-heavy workloads. The profile is appropriate for network-bound microservices, static web serving (measured at 6.49 GB/sec throughput), front-end API gateways, single-threaded batch processing, and lightweight caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores at 3.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It includes no integrated local storage and no hardware GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes for block storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the c6in.xlarge demonstrates average single-core throughput, reflected in its Geekbench single-core score of 1518.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.49 GB/sec, while multi-core processing and memory bandwidth metrics reflect bottom-quartile results due to the modest 4-vCPU and 8.0 GB footprint. The hardware and network characteristics make this instance suitable for static web serving, network microservices, lightweight data transformation, and single-threaded batch computing.
